simple.meaning: עָקֵב (ʻâqêb) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a heel (as protuberant); hence, a track ; figuratively, the rear (of an army).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 13 times across Genesis, Joshua, Judges, Job, Psalms, and 2 more, beginning at Genesis 3:15. Its contexts include family, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָקֵב (H6119).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עָקֵב (ʻâqêb) / H6119 is traced through Genesis 3:15, Genesis 25:26, Genesis 49:17, Genesis 49:19 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a heel (as protuberant); hence, a track ; figuratively, the rear (of an army)
definitions.usage: heel, (horse-) hoof, last, lier in wait (by mistake for 6120 ), (foot-) step.
definitions.full: H6119. aqeb I. עָקֵב noun masculine heel, footprint, hinderpart (Arabic heel , figurative end (of a month), mark, sign, trace ; Aramaic עִקְבָּא , hell, footprint , figurative trace, mark (compare Wisdom 2:4 ᵑ6 Ecclus 13:26 HCT ᵑ6 ), also end, extremity ); — ׳ע absolute Gen 3:15 +, construct עֲקֵב 25:26 , plural construct עִקָבֵי Song 1:8 , עִקְּבֵי Gen 49:17 ; Judg 5:22 , עִקְּבוֺת Psa 77:20 ; 89:52 , etc.; — a. heel , of man, Gen 25:26 אָחִיו בַּעֲקֵב אֹחֶזֶת וְיָדוֺ , as object of attack from behind, 3:15 עָקֵב תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ וְאַתָּה , Job 18:9 בְּע ׳יאֹחֵז מַּח , Jer 13:22 עֲקֵבָ֑יִךְ נֶחְמְסוּ are treated violently, i.e. are rudely exposed (|| שׁוּלַיִךְ נִגְלוּ ); as instrument of attack, Psa 41:10 עָ עָלַי ׳הִגְדִּיל hath made great the heel against me , i.e. given me insidiously a great fall (figurative for taken some cruel advantage of me; compare ὑποσκελίζω ); of an animal, Gen 49:17 סוּם עִקְּבֵי הַנּשֵׁח , Judg 5:22 b. mark of heel, footprint , Song 1:8 הַצּאֹן בְּעִקְבֵי צְאִילָֿח , Psa 56:7 עֲקֵבַי יִשְׁמְרוּ they mark my footprints , i.e. watch me insidiously wherever I go 89:52 מְשִׁיחֶ֑ךָ עִקְּבוֺת ֵהרְפוּ אֲשֶׁר i.e. followed him mockingly, of ׳י (figurative) 77:20 נוֺדָ֑עוּ לֹא עִקְּבוֺתֶיךָ thy footprints were not known (the waters closing over them). c hinder-part, rear (of a troop of men), Gen 49:19 עָקֵב׃ יָגוּב וְהוּא (read אָשֵׁר ׃ עֲקֵבָם ) he will troop on their rear , Josh 8:13 עֲקֵבָם (compare Di).
